question: The income of Raman is ₹34,000. He saves 28% of his income. If his income increases by 11% and expenditure increases by 30%, then his savings will:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Income** = 100, **Savings** = 28, **Expenditure** = 72.

New Income = 111 | New Expenditure = 72 × 1.3 = 93.6

New Savings = 111 − 93.6 = 17.4

Change in Savings = 17.4 − 28 = −10.6 units

Value = (34000 ÷ 100) × (−10.6) = −3604

**∴ The correct answer is decrease by ₹3,604.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial Income = ₹34,000, Saving% = 28%, Income Increase = 11%, Expenditure Increase = 30%

**Formula Used:** Income = Expenditure + Savings

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c583f43607b77e16beddab9ed873232731f61510aa6b182bc07d02c07b9bb176.png] 

⇒ Initial **Savings** = 28% of 34,000 = 0.28 × 34,000 = ₹9,520

⇒ Initial **Expenditure** = 34,000 − 9,520 = ₹24,480

⇒ New **Income** = 34,000 × 111/100 = ₹37,740

⇒ New **Expenditure** = 24,480 × 130/100 = ₹31,824

⇒ New **Savings** = 37,740 − 31,824 = ₹5,916

⇒ Change in **Savings** = 5,916 − 9,520 = −₹3,604

**∴ The correct answer is decrease by ₹3,604.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change in Savings

The percentage change in savings can also be found using the weighted average of percentage changes in expenditure and savings to equal the percentage change in income.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value changes by a% and then by b%, the net change is given by (a + b + ab/100)%.

Base Change Property

When income and expenditure change at different rates, the savings change is highly sensitive to the initial savings-to-expenditure ratio.
